points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 王维出生于太原祁县（今山西祁县），后迁居蒲州（今山西永济）。他自幼聪颖过人，九岁便能作诗，精通音律。父亲早逝，母亲崔氏信奉佛教，这对王维后来的思想产生了深远影响。少年时期，王维展现出非凡的文学才华，与弟弟王缙一同学习，兄弟情深。这段时期奠定了他深厚的文化素养和艺术基础，为他日后的诗歌创作和仕途生涯埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: Wang Wei was born in Qi County, Taiyuan (present-day Shanxi Province), and later moved to Pu Prefecture (present-day Yongji, Shanxi). He showed exceptional talent from a young age, composing poetry at age nine and mastering music. His father died early, and his mother, Lady Cui, was a devout Buddhist, which profoundly influenced his later thoughts. During his youth, Wang Wei demonstrated extraordinary literary talent, studying alongside his younger brother Wang Jin. This period laid the foundation for his profound cultural literacy and artistic abilities, foreshadowing his future poetic career and official path.

points.title: 科举入仕
points.description: 717年，王维来到长安，开始仕途生涯。他凭借才华和家族背景，很快在文人圈中崭露头角。721年，王维进士及第，被任命为太乐丞，负责宫廷音乐事务。这一时期，他创作了大量描绘宫廷生活和自然景色的诗歌，如《九月九日忆山东兄弟》等，展现了他早期诗歌风格的特点。在长安的仕途初期，王维结识了许多著名文人，如孟浩然、李白等，这些交往丰富了他的文学视野，也为他日后的创作提供了灵感。
points.descriptionEn: In 717, Wang Wei arrived in Chang'an and began his official career. With his talent and family background, he quickly stood out in literary circles. In 721, Wang Wei passed the imperial examination and was appointed as Tai Le Cheng, responsible for court music affairs. During this period, he wrote numerous poems depicting court life and natural scenery, such as 'Thinking of My Brothers in Shandong on the Ninth Day of the Ninth Month,' showcasing the characteristics of his early poetic style. In the early stages of his official career in Chang'an, Wang Wei met many famous literary figures such as Meng Haoran and Li Bai, whose enriching broadened his literary perspective and provided inspiration for his future works.

points.title: 仕途起伏
points.description: 721年后，王维的仕途经历多次起伏。他曾因伶人舞狮事件被贬济州（今山东济宁），后调任凉州（今甘肃武威），担任河西节度使判官。这段经历使他有机会接触边塞风光和军旅生活，创作了《使至塞上》等著名边塞诗。735年，王维被召回长安，任右拾遗、监察御史等职。737年，张九龄执政时，王维受到重用，但张九龄被贬后，王维也受到牵连。这一时期，他的诗歌风格逐渐从早期的华丽转向内敛，开始融入更多禅宗思想，创作了《山居秋暝》等代表作。
points.descriptionEn: After 721, Wang Wei's official career experienced several fluctuations. He was demoted to Jizhou (present-day Jining, Shandong) due to an incident involving court performers dancing with lions, and later transferred to Liangzhou (present-day Wuwei, Gansu) serving as a judge for the Hexi Jiedushi. This experience allowed him to experience frontier scenery and military life, leading to the creation of famous frontier poems like 'Journey to the Frontier.' In 735, Wang Wei was recalled to Chang'an and served as You Shi Yi, Jian Cha Shi, and other positions. When Zhang Jiuling was in power, Wang Wei was valued, but after Zhang's demotion, Wang Wei was also implicated. During this period, his poetic style gradually shifted from the ornate of his early years to a more restrained expression, beginning to incorporate more Chan Buddhist thought, creating representative works like 'Autumn Dusk in the Mountain Abode.'

points.title: 隐居创作
points.description: 741年后，王维在终南山和辋川（今陕西蓝田）购置田产，过着半官半隐的生活。他在辋川别业中修建亭台楼阁，种植花草树木，与好友裴迪、孟浩然等人吟诗作画，过着闲适的生活。这一时期是王维创作的黄金时期，他创作了大量描绘山水田园的诗歌，如《辋川集》中的二十首诗，以及《鹿柴》、《竹里馆》等名篇。这些诗歌以简洁的语言描绘自然景色，融入禅宗思想，形成了独特的'诗中有画，画中有诗'的艺术风格。王维还精通绘画，尤其擅长山水画，被后人誉为'南宗画派'的鼻祖。
points.descriptionEn: After 741, Wang Wei purchased property in Zhongnan Mountain and Wangchuan (present-day Lantian, Shaanxi), living a semi-official, semi-hermit life. In his Wangchuan Villa, he built pavilions and towers, planted flowers and trees, and recited poetry and painted with friends like Pei Di and Meng Haoran, leading a leisurely existence. This period was the golden age of Wang Wei's creative output. He wrote numerous poems depicting landscapes and rural life, such as the twenty poems in the 'Wangchuan Collection,' and famous pieces like 'Deer Park' and 'Bamboo Grove Studio.' These poems used concise language to depict natural scenery while incorporating Chan Buddhist thought, forming a unique artistic style of 'poetry in painting, painting in poetry.' Wang Wei was also an accomplished painter, especially skilled in landscape painting, later revered as the founder of the 'Southern School' of painting.

points.title: 安史之乱
points.description: 755年，安史之乱爆发，王维被叛军俘虏，被迫接受伪职。757年，唐军收复长安，王维因曾接受伪职被下狱，幸得其弟王缙削官相救，才得以免死，被贬为太子中允。761年，王维在长安逝世，享年61岁。安史之乱是王维人生的重大转折点，他经历了从朝廷重臣到阶下囚的巨大落差，这使他的思想更加超脱，对佛教的信仰也更加虔诚。晚年，他被称为'诗佛'，将诗歌创作与佛教修行紧密结合，创作了《辋川集》等充满禅意的作品，对后世文人产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 755, the An Lushan Rebellion broke out, and Wang Wei was captured by the rebel forces, forced to accept a position in the puppet regime. In 757, when the Tang army recaptured Chang'an, Wang Wei was imprisoned for having served in the puppet government. Fortunately, his younger brother Wang Jin reduced his own official rank to save him, sparing him from death and demoting him to Crown Prince's Assistant. In 761, Wang Wei died in Chang'an at the age of 61. The An Lushan Rebellion was a major turning point in Wang Wei's life. He experienced the dramatic fall from a high court official to a prisoner, which made his thoughts more detached and his Buddhist faith more devout. In his later years, he was known as the 'Poet-Buddha,' closely integrating poetry creation with Buddhist practice, producing works like the 'Wangchuan Collection' filled with Zen wisdom, exerting a profound influence on later literati.

appraisal.zh: 王维被尊为「诗佛」，其山水诗以简净语言写自然而深含禅意，兼擅绘画，被奉为南宗画派之祖，「诗中有画，画中有诗」成为中国美学的重要命题，他也被视为文人「穷则独善其身」理想人格的典范。不过也有研究者指出，他在安史之乱中接受伪职有亏气节，诗作多囿于个人情感与自然描写，缺乏社会关怀，隐逸生活亦被讥为逃避现实。这些异议并未动摇其诗画合一的经典地位。
appraisal.en: Wang Wei is revered as the "Poet-Buddha": his landscape poems depict nature in spare language steeped in Zen, and as a painter he is honored as the founder of the Southern School, with "poetry in painting, painting in poetry" becoming a key tenet of Chinese aesthetics. He is also seen as a model of the literati ideal of cultivating virtue in adversity. Yet researchers note that accepting office under the rebels during the An Lushan Rebellion compromised his integrity, that his poems dwell on personal feeling and nature without social concern, and that his reclusion has been called escapism. These objections have not shaken his classic status.

supporter.zh: 王维被誉为'诗佛'，是中国文学史上最伟大的诗人之一。他的诗歌融合了儒、释、道三家思想，创造了独特的艺术境界。他的山水诗以简洁的语言描绘自然，蕴含深刻禅意，开创了中国诗歌的新境界。作为画家，他开创了'南宗画派'，对后世绘画影响深远。王维的作品不仅艺术价值极高，更体现了中国文人对自然与精神境界的追求，成为中国传统文化的重要组成部分。
supporter.en: Wang Wei, revered as the 'Poet-Buddha,' is one of the greatest poets in Chinese literary history. His poetry integrates Confucian, Buddhist, and Taoist philosophies, creating a unique artistic realm. His landscape poems, with concise language depicting nature and profound Zen insights, pioneered a new horizon in Chinese poetry. As a painter, he founded the 'Southern School' of painting, exerting far-reaching influence on later generations. Wang Wei's works possess not only high artistic value but also embody Chinese literati's pursuit of nature and spiritual realms, becoming an essential part of traditional Chinese culture.

critic.zh: 批评者认为王维在安史之乱期间接受伪职的行为有失气节，违背了儒家'忠君爱国'的价值观。他的诗歌虽然艺术成就高，但内容多局限于个人情感和自然描写，缺乏对社会的深刻关怀和批判精神。此外，他的隐逸生活被视为逃避现实，未能积极承担知识分子的社会责任。这些批评反映了传统文人对'气节'的重视，以及对文学应具有社会功能的期望。
critic.en: Critics argue that Wang Wei's acceptance of a position in the puppet regime during the An Lushan Rebellion showed a lack of integrity, violating Confucian values of 'loyalty to the ruler and love for the country.' Although his poetry achieves high artistic merit, its content is often limited to personal emotions and natural descriptions, lacking deep social concern and critical spirit. Furthermore, his hermit life is seen as escapism, failing to actively fulfill the social responsibilities of intellectuals. These criticisms reflect traditional literati's emphasis on 'integrity' and their expectation that literature should have social functions.

objective.zh: 从历史与流行文化视角看，王维已成为中国传统文化的重要符号，代表了中国文人'达则兼济天下，穷则独善其身'的理想人格。他的诗歌与绘画艺术相互影响，形成了'诗中有画，画中有诗'的独特美学风格，对中国艺术发展产生了深远影响。在当代，王维的作品被广泛研究，其融合自然与禅意的艺术理念对现代人的精神生活仍有启示意义。王维的形象超越了单纯的诗人或画家，成为中国传统文化中'诗画合一'美学的典范。
objective.en: From a historical and popular culture perspective, Wang Wei has become an important symbol of traditional Chinese culture, representing the ideal personality of Chinese literati: 'when successful, benefit the world; when in adversity, cultivate one's own virtue.' His poetry and painting mutually influenced each other, forming a unique aesthetic style of 'poetry in painting, painting in poetry,' exerting profound influence on the development of Chinese art. In contemporary times, Wang Wei's works are widely studied, and his artistic philosophy integrating nature and Zen still offers inspiration for modern spiritual life. Wang Wei's image transcends the simple identity of poet or painter, becoming a model of the 'unity of poetry and painting' aesthetic in traditional Chinese culture.

self.zh: 行到水穷处，坐看云起时。
self.en: When I reach the end of the water, I sit and watch the clouds rise.
